The video's purpose is to collect and organise a science's information so it is easy to understand, digest and remember. A student who writes the video's answer could be marked down by the AI marker.

findings.issue: The match teaches different meanings from the video. The video says matn comes from 'to strengthen and solidify' and nazm from 'to organise and collect'. The draft has 'Text' and 'Poem/verse'. It also adds sharh/shaarih, which the video never mentions. The key isn't false Arabic, but students are tested on wordings they weren't taught and on two terms they never met.

to.right: The one who authors a nazm (the collector / organiser)
The one who authors a matn

findings.issue: The rubric marks 'Tajweed' as the answer, but the video says the opposite: the Ten Principles is not a Tajweed text. It is a general text whose principles apply to any science, and the course applies them to Tajweed. A student who answers as the video teaches would be marked wrong.

proposed.to: It is not a Tajweed text: it is a general/generic text whose ten principles apply to any science (in this course they are applied to Tajweed). Accept 'any science' / 'general'.

findings.issue: The rubric gives 1 mark for 'the subject matter is the words/letters of the Qur'an', which the video never says. The video gives four structured contents: makhaarij, sifaat, the Tajweed rules (ikhfaa, idghaam, iqlaab...), and stopping/starting with its emphasis. A student who lists all four could lose a mark. The prompt's '(subject matter)' also steers students toward the untaught answer.

findings.issue: The key is correct by standard teaching, but one correct option ('heavy or light pronunciation ... e.g. of raa'') sits right next to the video's example of a RIGHT, which is isti'laa' (heaviness inherent to the letter). Students may reasonably hesitate. The video's own example of a due is the vowel on the letter, so using it keeps the key tied to what was taught.
findings.evidence: Video 3: rights = makhraj + inherent characteristics, 'for example ... al-isti'la'; dues = 'the harakah that's on the letter ... a fatha, a damma, a kasra, it can be a sakin. And also ... madd or idgham'

proposed.from: Heavy or light pronunciation (tafkheem/tarqeeq) that depends on the vowel, e.g. of raa'
proposed.to: The vowel on the letter (fathah, dammah, kasrah or sukoon), which changes from word to word

findings.issue: The second rubric mark ('a clear mistake (lahn jaliyy) and therefore sinful') comes from a different video. In this lesson the point is that changing a letter changes the word's meaning, which then affects the tafseer of the ayah (qalb to kalb, heart to dog). A student who gives the lesson's answer would get only 1 of 2 marks.
findings.evidence: Video 5: 'we say kalb instead of qalb ... changed the meaning of the word from heart to dog ... that will affect the tafsir of that particular ayah'

proposed.to: So the understanding/tafseer of the ayah is affected (e.g. qalb 'heart' becomes kalb 'dog'); also accept: it is a clear mistake (lahn jaliyy) and sinful

findings.issue: The order is historically correct: Hafs took the recitation from 'Aasim. But no video in this series teaches 'Aasim or Hafs or their order. Episode 6 does teach the steps between the Prophet (ﷺ) and today: the Companions, then their students, and so on. Testing those keeps the order inside what was taught, and it is closer to last year's question, which asked for the last three links (the Prophet, Jibreel, Allah).

findings.issue: The verse reference is right (73:4 contains وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا). But this episode quotes the verse without defining tarteel. summary: The structure is sound: all 7 totals match, every rubric adds up to its points, and every mcq has exactly one correct option. The draft was written without the videos, so this review fetched the YouTube auto-captions for all 7 episodes (rev_mabadi/) and checked each key against them. Most keys match what the teacher says: as-Sabbaan (d. 1792), the order of the ten principles, the fruits, the related sciences (tafseer, qiraa'aat, waqf; not fiqh), the reason the theory was written down, fard 'ayn for practice and fard kifayah for theory, and the chain ending Prophet, Jibreel, Allah. Two keys contradict the video: HW2 Q5 (the video says the Ten Principles is NOT a Tajweed text) and HW3 Q5 (the four structured contents, not 'the words of the Qur'an'). Several rubrics and the HW1 match use textbook wording or terms the course never teaches, which risks the AI marker penalising correct answers. Arabic names and terms are dropped in the captions (the theory founder, the author-of-a-matn word), so those still need the teacher.
